baselineAssumptions.context: Ecological studies focusing on vegetation organization.
baselineAssumptions.description: The method assumes a fixed minimum sample size threshold for achieving structural stability in ecological analyses.

frames.description: Frame focusing on the methods and concepts used in ecological analysis, particularly for community organization.
frames.evidenceSnippet: "This method and this concept are illustrated by two examples: the first is relative to the determination of the optimal sample size in a vegetation study and the second, to the verification of the value of this choice." (Resumo)
frames.label: Ecological Analysis

declaredActions.statement: Illustrating the method and concept through two examples: determining optimal sample size and verifying its value.

declaredProblems.statement: Determining an appropriate sample size for ecological analyses.

expectedEffects.statement: Improved accuracy and reliability of ecological analyses in vegetation studies.

authorInterpretations: This method and this concept are illustrated by two examples: the first is relative to the determination of the optimal sample size in a vegetation study and the second, to the verification of the value of this choice.

possibleReadings: The study provides guidelines for determining an appropriate sample size to ensure structural stability in ecological analyses.
The method can be used to both determine the minimum required sample size and validate its effectiveness in different vegetation studies.
